0.3.9.headline: Windows titlebar actually works now, and Linux updates stop breaking installs
changes: Windows: minimize / maximize / close buttons AND dragging all work. v0.3.8 was missing two things: (1) ACL grants for the start_dragging / minimize / close / set_focus window commands (Tauri 2 requires explicit permission per command, and only a few were allowed by default), and (2) the titlebar buttons were bubbling their mousedown up to the drag region, so clicking a button started a window drag instead. Both fixed — ACL grants added, buttons now stop event propagation before the drag handler sees them.

Linux: the v0.3.8 AppImage linked against system libwebkit2gtk-4.1 but CI accidentally bundled the library file itself. The bundled webkit has its helper-process path hardcoded at compile time (Ubuntu's /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/webkit2gtk-4.1/...), which doesn't exist on Arch / Fedora / NixOS — so the AppImage would launch then the renderer crashed spawning WebKitNetworkProcess. v0.3.9 is packaged with appimagetool directly (bypassing linuxdeploy's ldd-copying step), so NOTHING is bundled. dlopen resolves webkit/gtk from your host system at runtime, and the helper paths match your distro's own layout.
One-click in-place auto-update on Linux now works end-to-end with the new AppImage.
0.3.9.footer: If your v0.3.8 Linux install broke after the auto-update, delete the installed AppImage and grab the v0.3.9 one from app.aftercalls.io/downloads. Going forward, v0.3.9 → v0.3.10 will upgrade cleanly via the Install pill.

0.3.8.headline: One-click Linux updates, Windows titlebar really working, no more phantom windows, and an audio download button
changes: Linux: one-click in-place auto-update actually works now. We stopped shipping Tauri's bundled-webkit AppImage (the one that crashed on Arch/NixOS/some Ubuntu combos) and build a slim AppImage instead that dynamic-links to your distro's own libwebkit2gtk-4.1 + libgtk-3. Install the v0.3.8 AppImage once, and from then on updates arrive as a pill in the top bar exactly like Windows — click Install, the app swaps itself and relaunches. Requires libwebkit2gtk-4.1 + libgtk-3 installed on the host (preinstalled on Debian/Ubuntu; one package on Arch/Fedora).
Linux on .deb / .rpm / tarball installs: the built-in updater still can't swap those in place, but you'll see the same "Get it ↗" notification pill pointing at /downloads that v0.3.7 shipped.

Call detail: new Download button next to the playback-rate button on both the app and the web portal. Downloads whichever track is selected (Everyone / You / Others) as an .opus file named after the call, which plays in Windows Media Player, macOS, VLC, and any modern browser without needing a codec.

Windows: the titlebar drag AND the min / max / close buttons both work. v0.3.7 swapped the drag approach and accidentally broke both. Back on the Tauri drag-region path with a small pointer-events tweak so clicks on the SVG icons actually reach the buttons.

Linux: opening the app from the tray while a call was active sometimes spawned two or three phantom copies of the window. Added single-instance handling so a second launch re-shows the existing window instead of starting a fresh process, and skipped the redundant show() call when the window is already visible (which was the trigger on Hyprland / sway).

0.3.7.headline: Linux update pill, working Windows titlebar buttons, and a less-naggy vault toggle
changes: Linux: the app now checks for new releases in the background and shows a "v0.x.y available — Get it ↗" pill in the top bar when one is out. Clicking it opens the downloads page in your browser so you can grab the tarball or .deb. (The built-in updater still can't swap a Linux binary in place — the AppImage's bundled webkit crashes on too many distros to rely on it — but at least you'll know there's something to update to.)

Windows: the minimize / maximize / close buttons in the titlebar actually respond to clicks now. The previous release made the titlebar draggable but accidentally swallowed the clicks on those buttons.

Settings → Obsidian vault: flipping the switch off saves immediately — no Save button required. The Save button also hides itself when the feature is off, instead of sitting there looking like unfinished work.

0.3.6.headline: A handful of polish fixes you'll notice immediately
changes: Calls list groups calls by your local day instead of UTC. Calls recorded late evening were drifting to the next day (or the previous one) depending on your timezone. Now Today is actually today.
The "Saved" card after a call finishes is cleaner — one tap to open the call on the web portal, regardless of whether you use the Obsidian vault. The old path-and-vault-note line is gone.
Windows: the dark titlebar is draggable again — grab it anywhere empty to move the window.
Settings → Obsidian vault: the enable/disable checkbox is now an obvious on/off slider, so it's clear at a glance which state you're in.

0.3.5.headline: Obsidian is now optional, and Windows has a proper dark titlebar
changes: Obsidian vault is opt-in per machine. Settings → Obsidian vault (this machine) has a toggle, folder picker, and clients-subfolder field. Leave it off on machines where your vault isn't available; pipeline completes without writing a note, nothing fails.
If you enable the vault but the write fails, the rest of the pipeline (transcribe, summarize, save to cloud) still succeeds — the error gets logged but doesn't fail the call.
Windows: native titlebar is replaced with an integrated dark one. Double-click to maximize, drag to move, and min/max/close buttons match the app palette.
0.3.5.footer: v0.3.4 was the intended titlebar release but its CI build broke on a CSS regression — v0.3.5 is the same release with the build fixed.

0.3.4.headline: Windows finally looks like it belongs in the dark theme
changes: Windows: native titlebar is replaced with an integrated dark one. Double-click the top bar to maximize, drag to move, and the min/max/close buttons match the app palette (close still turns Windows-red on hover, as it should).
Linux/macOS: unchanged — GTK chrome and native macOS traffic lights stay intact.

0.3.3.headline: Windows finally captures the other side of the call
changes: Windows: system audio (the person on the other end of a Zoom/Teams/phone call) is now captured alongside your mic via WASAPI loopback. Uses the cpal audio library the mic was already on, so no new drivers, no config — the call just records both sides.
Calls where one track didn't get uploaded (corner cases, crashes, mid-session agent swaps) no longer fail the whole pipeline — the backend skips missing tracks and transcribes whatever did arrive.
Linux: if the agent is force-killed mid-recording, the system-audio child process now dies with it instead of becoming an orphan that silently eats disk.

0.3.2.headline: session tokens stay fresh, and the summary reads like something you'd paste into an email
changes: Fixed a bug where recordings made more than an hour after signing in failed with a 401. The agent now refreshes its session token automatically when it's about to expire — the same way it already did for read-only requests. If you hit this, signing out and back in was the workaround; you shouldn't need to anymore.
Summaries and action items now refer to you by your first name in the third person, not "You." So you can copy/paste straight into an email to a customer or teammate without rewriting.
Transcript lines you spoke also get labeled with your first name instead of "You."
0.3.2.footer: Calls recorded before this update still show the old wording — the new prompt only runs on fresh recordings. Re-summarize (#19) is in the queue so we can apply the new prompt to older calls too.

0.3.1.headline: the Windows upload actually works this time, and your transcript clicks go where you meant
changes: Windows: call uploads no longer fail with a 500. The agent's WAV-fallback path was sending a content-type that didn't match the signed URL, which Spaces was rejecting silently. Fixed.
Call detail (agent): clicking a transcript line now seeks to the correct timestamp every time. Audio loads fast on long calls too — we stopped round-tripping the whole file through fetch + blob.
Summaries hold a more consistent shape across calls — past tense, third person, action items as short imperative phrases.
Auto-detect end-of-call timeout dropped from 20s to 5s; the app will prompt to end a recording much sooner when you stop talking.
App checks for updates about once an hour while running, not just on launch.
Record page says "Syncing to cloud" instead of the more technical "Syncing to backend."
Small UI: title chips are now the same size, and the record page stacks "Recording · Transcribing" when you start a new call while the previous one is still processing.

0.3.0.headline: the one where calls stop disappearing and the portal catches up
changes: Windows: recordings stop failing after "Stop". The agent now falls back to uploading WAV when ffmpeg isn't installed, so the transcription service can actually fetch the audio.
Renaming a speaker now rewrites the transcript, summary, action items, and participants in one go — no more "Speaker A" stuck in the summary after you've renamed them.

Participants moved to the top of the call view (above Summary) so you rename before you read. Speaker names in the summary and action items are tinted with each person's chip color so you can scan them at a glance.
Web portal caught up to the agent: waveform, highlights (create/edit/delete/auto-detect), speaker editing, delete-with-confirm, copy buttons, and a themed /downloads page.

Admin: self-service profile + password from Settings, invite + manage teammates from Team, /admin/vocab for org-wide spelling corrections and word boost. Calls are now scoped to you by default, with a "My calls / All team" toggle for admins.
Recording status card trimmed — no more on-screen file paths.
Post-update welcome modal now fires after sign-in so it can greet you by name.
0.3.0.footer: Known: the Linux AppImage can still crash on some distros (bundled webkit2gtk fork). Fix is in progress — use the .deb if you're on Debian/Ubuntu.

0.2.1.headline: a few fixes that make the app actually work on fresh installs
changes: Fresh installs on Windows can now sign in — the agent creates a default config pointing at the production backend when one doesn't exist yet.
Call detail waveforms render everywhere again. A backend deadlock in peaks generation was silently leaving every non-trivial recording with no waveform.
Vocab settings (spelling corrections + word boost) moved to the web portal under Admin → Vocab. Admins manage them once for the whole team.
You'll see this welcome popup right after signing in, not just on first launch.
0.2.1.footer: If you missed the v0.2.0 notes, open Settings → About or ask us — we can resurface them.

0.2.0.headline: Account controls, a real waveform, and a bug fix you'll be glad to hear about
changes: You can now edit your display name, email, and password from Settings in the web portal. Email changes go through a verification link.
Admins can edit teammates: rename, change email, change role, or trigger a password reset — all from the Team page.
Invited users now show up as "pending" in Team, so you can see who hasn't accepted yet.
Call detail now renders a real waveform, thanks to server-side peak generation. No more flat line.
The recording timer stays in sync after you close the app to tray and reopen it mid-recording.
Deleting a call shows a proper confirm dialog instead of the browser's default.
Fixed a bug where finished calls were silently losing their transcript and summary after the vault note was saved. Your future recordings will land complete.
0.2.0.footer: Heads up: older recordings in the portal may still be blank from that last bug. We can help recover from local vault notes if you need to — just reach out.
